subject: SlateWave: migration economics, price-match mechanics, and packaging questions
messages:
From: Nina Patel <nina.patel@slatewave.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com
Cc: contracts@slatewave.com, Tom Briggs <t.briggs@slatewave.com>
Date: Fri, 27 Aug 2026 09:15:00 -0700
Subject: SlateWave RFP: migration credits & price-match question

Hi Aditya —

Thanks for the quick intro this week. We're finishing up an internal bid for our inference stack and have a couple of questions before we move to procurement:

1) Competitive price-match: our incumbent (VeraScale) has offered an effective unit price of $0.0009/token with a three-month on-ramp credit. Can Redwood provide a like-for-like price-match or an equivalent economics package?

2) Migration credits & packaging: we need clarity on what you can make available for migration (egress credits, hands-on engineering time, staged billing). We care about minimizing one-time lift and preserving predictable run-rate.

3) Deployment mode: we currently run in a hybrid model (sensitive workloads on dedicated in our VPC, others on hosted). What packaging (Dedicated vs Hosted) do you recommend for a comparable run-rate while keeping latency <120ms for 1-2k QPS peaks?

Attached is our RFP excerpt for quick context (see requested metrics). Appreciate a short written response and a ballpark commercial so we can move to our procurement team.

Best,
Nina Patel
Head of Procurement, SlateWave
---
SlateWave | procurement@slatewave.com
From: aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com <aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com>

Cc: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
Date: Fri, 27 Aug 2026 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: SlateWave RFP: migration credits & price-match question

Hi Nina —

Thanks for sharing the RFP excerpt — useful context. High-level answers and a few clarifying asks below:

Competitive price-match: we can align to a comparable effective unit price for a 12-month committed arrangement, dependent on usage bands and whether you need Dedicated capacity guarantees. As a starting point, we can present a price-match option that matches your $0.0009/token effective rate for the first 6 months if SlateWave commits to a 12-month minimum and a predictable monthly committed volume.

Migration credits & packaging: we typically offer a two-part credit structure for switch deals: (a) a one-time migration credit that offsets egress and cutover costs (usually scoped as either a fixed dollar amount or up to X months of committed spend), and (b) a PS (professional services) hours bucket for the onboarding runbook and integration (engineer-led). I've attached a cost_breakdown_sheet.xlsx with a couple of scenarios (low, baseline, high).

Deployment mode recommendation: for mixed workloads like yours we recommend a small Dedicated pool for PII-sensitive flows plus Redwood Hosted API for high-volume, non-sensitive traffic. That preserves latency SLAs for sensitive traffic while giving you cost elasticity. In practice: Dedicated for steady-state high-SLA flows + Hosted for bursty unpredictable traffic works well and keeps average token cost lower.

Quick clarifying asks so we can firm numbers:
- Current average monthly token consumption and 95th percentile daily peak;
- Any hard SLA requirements beyond latency (e.g., blackout windows, throughput SLAs);
- Whether data residency/VPC-only control plane is required.

I'll loop in Marissa (commercial) and Jonas (solutions) with a draft commercial and redline SOW to follow. Attached: cost_breakdown_sheet.xlsx (ballparks only).

Cheers,
Aditya Rao
Senior Account Executive | Redwood Inference
aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com | +1 415-555-0198
From: marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com <marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com>
To: aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com, jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sat, 28 Aug 2026 08:40:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: SlateWave concession framing and redline

Aditya / Jonas —

Quick internal note before we finalize the external offer:

- Recommendation: offer a formal price-match matrix tied to committed bands (3 tiers). Match VeraScale's effective $0.0009/token for months 1-6 on a 12-month commit, then step to $0.00105/token thereafter unless they expand volume.
- Migration credit: propose a $25k fixed migration credit + 40 hours of SWEs for onboarding (PS). That covers egress and initial integration for most customers of this size.
- Packaging: include an explicit Dedicated/Hosted hybrid clause in the SOW so we can autopilot routing and have fallbacks; this reduces their perceived migration risk.
- Approval: finance and revenue ops signoff on $25k credit and 40 PS hours under DEAL-5721. Any larger concession needs CRO-level approval.

Attached: redline_SlateWave_SOW_2026.docx (with hybrid clause and explicit acceptance criteria).

Marissa Cole
Head of Commercial | Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com
From: jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com <jonas_weber@redwoodinference.com>
To: Nina Patel <nina.patel@slatewave.com>
Cc: aditya_rao@redwoodinference.com, marissa_cole@redwoodinference.com, contracts@slatewave.com
Date: Sun, 29 Aug 2026 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Redwood commercial proposal: SlateWave price-match & onboarding package

Hi Nina / Tom —

Thanks for the RFP excerpt and the openness on incumbent economics. Per Aditya and Marissa's input, here's the formal offer for procurement to review: 

1) Price-match: Redwood will match the incumbent effective rate of $0.0009/token for the first 6 months under a 12-month committed term with the following committed bands:
   - Tier A (>= 10M tokens/mo): $0.00085/token (first 6 months), $0.00100/token thereafter
   - Tier B (3-10M tokens/mo): $0.0009/token (first 6 months), $0.00105/token thereafter
   - Tier C (<3M tokens/mo): $0.00100/token (first 6 months), $0.00120/token thereafter
2) Migration credits & PS: one-time $25,000 migration credit to offset egress and cutover costs + up to 40 hours of complimentary professional services (engineer time) for integration, on-call runbook creation, and a staged roll-out plan.
3) Packaging & SLA: hybrid deployment (Dedicated pool + Hosted fallback) included. We'll document routing rules and latency targets in the SOW. Standard SLA applies; addendum for higher SLA targets available as an upgrade.
4) Next steps: we attached two files — SlateWave_RFP_response_v3.pdf (commercial summary) and redline_SlateWave_SOW_2026.docx (SOW with acceptance criteria). Please confirm the committed monthly band you expect so we can issue a finalized order form.

If SlateWave can confirm by COB Sep 6 we can lock in the migration credit and the 6-month introductory pricing. If you need a larger credit or longer introductory match we'll escalate for CRO approval.

Best,
Jonas Weber
Solutions Director | Redwood Inference

Appreciate the clarity and the written offer. SlateWave is encouraged by the price-match matrix and the migration credit. A few quick items from procurement/legal: 

- We'll share exact monthly token bands by EOD Wed (we're finalizing traffic gating for Q4).
- Legal will run the redline on the SOW and get back with minor edits (primarily around data retention and audit log export windows).
- Can we schedule a 30-minute exec call (VP Eng + Head of Product from our side) to walk the hybrid routing and failover behavior? Tom and I are available Thu/Fri afternoon PST.

If everything looks good on the redline, procurement is prepared to move to signature and request that the migration credit be applied to the first invoice.

Thanks — looking forward to next steps.

Nina Patel
